subject: Climate & Environment
title: Solar Farms vs. Rooftop Solar
description: Learn Solar Farms vs. Rooftop Solar in one minute.

hook.text: A utility-scale solar farm can power 100,000 homes. A rooftop system powers just one.

buildup.text: Solar farms use cheap land in sunny deserts and benefit from massive economies of scale.

discovery.text: Rooftop solar skips transmission losses and lets homeowners generate their own power.

twist.text: Both compete for investment. Farms win on cost. Rooftops win on independence.

climax.text: The best strategy is both — large farms for baseload, rooftops for distributed resilience.

punchline.text: Big or small, every panel steals a watt from fossil fuels.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of rooftop solar over solar farms?

details.summary: Utility-scale solar farms generate power at lower cost per kilowatt-hour thanks to economies of scale and optimal panel positioning. Rooftop solar avoids land use, reduces transmission losses, and empowers homeowners, but costs more per watt and faces shading and orientation constraints.
details.whyItMatters: Both approaches have vital roles in the energy transition. Understanding their trade-offs helps communities and policymakers design the most effective solar deployment strategies.
takeaways: Solar farms are cheaper per watt due to economies of scale
Rooftop panels reduce transmission losses and land impact
Most decarbonization scenarios rely on a mix of both

faq.question: How much land do solar farms require?
faq.answer: A typical solar farm needs about five to seven acres per megawatt. A gigawatt-scale farm might cover 5,000 acres. Dual-use approaches like agrivoltaics allow farming beneath elevated panels, reducing land-use conflicts.

faq.question: Is rooftop solar worth the higher cost?
faq.answer: For homeowners, rooftop solar can eliminate electricity bills and provide energy independence. It also reduces strain on transmission infrastructure. With battery storage and net metering, the higher panel cost is often offset by avoided grid charges.
